chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: The Clark Hotel and Washington and Central ballroom
summary: The older small Clark Hotel and its Annex, and the Washington and Central ballroom, number one black dance hall.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And then at Washington (inaudible) and Central there was the Clark--

The Clark Hotel was there for years and years. It was a much older place. It was next door to what was the number one black dance hall of the day, which was aptly named Washington and Central. That was the name of the ballroom upstairs. The big bands of that day worked in Washington and Central Ballroom.
Would Well, the Clark went into (inaudible) after--
It was right next door -- after what? the Somerville?
It was operating as a black hotel?
Yes, but it was a very small hotel. It didn't have 20 rooms in it.
Then that was -- was it built by the Clark family or just operated by the Clark family?

I don't think it was built by the Clark family at all. It was operated by Mr. Clark. He also built an annex a couple years later, around 1932. He built an annex a half-block from there on the other side of the street, called The Clark Annex.
